Amelia —

Thanks for sending the redlines and the timeline. We're happy to work through these items. Quick responses to the three bullets:

- Net terms: Redwood standard is Net 30. For enterprise customers we can consider Net 45 after credit review; Net 60 is possible but usually requires credit approval and a financing fee.
- Taxes: Our typical position is to invoice gross (no withholding) and provide tax residency paperwork where required; we can discuss alternatives if NuWare cannot gross-up.
- Invoicing cadence: We can invoice quarterly with an annual minimum commit and a quarterly true-up — that structure is common.

I've looped in Kar as the commercial lead and Lauren from Legal to review the redline. Kar and I can join a call with your procurement team tomorrow (Jul 8) at 10:30am PT if that works to speed this up.

I've attached a short commercial summary that maps NuWare's redlines to our recommended responses.

Priyom / Kar —

Thanks — 10:30am PT tomorrow works. A few clarifications ahead of the call so we can surface the right people:

- Net terms flexibility: NuWare can stretch to Net 45 if Redwood can commit to a 45-day payment plan without additional fee. Net 60 will only be possible if Redwood agrees to either a small financing fee or if we set up a milestone/PO schedule tied to cashflow.
- Withholding/statutory taxes: Our tax team prefers that vendors accept invoice net of statutory withholding where applicable. If Redwood's policy is gross invoicing, we will need a statement of tax residency or a W-8/W-9 equivalent to support our tax team.
- PO requirement: Procurement will need a formal, signed Order Form and a billing contact to generate the PO. They will not approve invoices without a PO number.

Attached an updated redline with tax clause highlighted (NuWare_OrderForm_v3_redlines_highlighted.pdf). Procurement joining tomorrow: Michael Keane (michael.keane@nuware.com) and Contracts inbox.

Amelia —

Great to meet earlier. Following up with Redwood's commercial position so you have it in writing ahead of procurement PO routing:

Proposed commercial response (high level):
- Invoicing cadence: We can invoice quarterly with an annual minimum commit and a quarterly true-up. Quarterly invoices will include line items for the committed units and a true-up/credit line for usage variance.
- Minimum commit: Keep as annual MRR/usage commit (customer billed quarterly). If NuWare needs a fully quarterly-contractual minimum, we can discuss structuring as four quarterly minimums instead of a single annual anchor, but pricing will reflect higher variability.
- Net terms: Standard Net 30. For enterprise deals we can move to Net 45 following a credit check. Net 60 may be accepted on a case-by-case basis with a 1.5% financing fee on amounts outstanding beyond 45 days or an approved payment plan.
- Taxes/withholding: Redwood's standard is gross invoicing; customers handle withholding where required. Redwood will provide tax residency documentation (W-9/W-8) and can include language that NuWare will provide certificates of tax withholding when applicable.

Operational asks from us:
- Please confirm PO process and expected timing for a PO number once the Order Form is signed.
- Provide the billing contact and remit-to details you expect to see on invoices.
- If NuWare expects Redwood to gross-up for withholding, specify the jurisdictions and expected rates so we can model the impact.

We can incorporate the above into a clean Order Form and limited redlines for legal to accept. Lauren — could you please review the redline items on tax language and net terms and advise on any alternative phrasing we should propose? We need legal sign-off to send the clean copy back to procurement by COB Monday (Jul 12).

Thanks — Kar

Lauren —

Can you review the attached NuWare redlines and Kar's commercial positions and provide wording we can send back to procurement? Key asks from commercial:

1) Invoicing & commits- Accept quarterly invoicing with an annual minimum commit and quarterly true-up. If NuWare insists on quarterly contractual minimums, flag pricing/vulnerability and propose optional language.
2) Net terms- Preferred: Net 45 post-credit check. Fallback: Allow Net 60 only with a 1.5% financing fee or an approved payment plan. We want language that gives sales flexibility without opening a precedent.
3) Taxes/withholding- Maintain gross invoicing stance. Add clause: Redwood will provide tax residency documentation on request and customer must notify Redwood if statutory withholding will apply and provide supporting certificates; include indemnity carveout for gross-up only if Redwood explicitly agrees in writing.
4) PO & operational- Confirm that procurement requires PO number before first invoice. Add a short billing contact and remit-to block in the order form.

Deadline: Procurement expects a clean copy by COB Monday (2026-07-12). If you can provide a redlined clean copy and a 2–3 line summary for commercial by EOD Monday, we can avoid delaying NuWare's onboarding.
